name: x6-step39-slot-sweep
description: ATTACK: can a run-jump actually take the low route past the column-39 step? The fixture declares lower-service low-approach -> low-step with verb 'run-jump' and routes dare-pocket through the same ground, but the chimney-left wall (39..40, y=5..10) puts a ceiling two tiles above that +1 step, so a jumping player's head enters cell (39,5) long before their feet clear cell (39,2). The passable band is feet in [2.98, 3.32] at the instant of the horizontal collision check - about one to two frames of a 16.5-tile/s jump. This script holds ArrowRight for the whole run (which pins the player at x=38.65 against the step) and tries eleven different jump hold lengths, 16ms through 500ms, 900ms apart, before the damage plane arrives. If maxX never exceeds ~38.7 and the run ends pinned, no jump duration opens the slot from the y=2 floor. Not an exhaustive proof - it sweeps hold length, not sub-frame press phase - but eleven failures plus the geometry is the case.
